artifacts.synopsis: TE Aaron Myers appealed Illiana Presbytery's decision to elevate his censures from indefinite suspension from office and from the Sacraments to excommunication and deposition, without any additional judicial process. The SJC sustained the appeal 21-1, holding that due process principles require some form of process before censure may be elevated, though the majority held that full de novo judicial process was not required; the sole dissent (RE Eggert) argued that Traditional Process under the BCO Rules of Discipline was required, and a concurring opinion (Sartorius) also argued for full BCO process.

artifacts.synopsis: Mr. Chandler Fozard complained that Fort Worth Presbyterian Church's policy restricting the integration of special case felons (including sex offenders) into the congregation violated Scripture. The SJC denied the complaint 20-1, finding the complainant had not demonstrated the Session violated Scripture or the Constitution, while criticizing the Session's arguments from BCO Preliminary Principles 1 and 2 as improper.

artifacts.title: Eliot Lee v. Korean Eastern
artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission sustained the complaints of TE Eliot Lee against Korean Eastern Presbytery (cases 2007-09 and 2007-10). KEP erred when it empowered the Pulpit Commission to act on behalf of the church session without proper consent, and erred when it filed a civil action against TE Lee to adjudicate ecclesiastical matters. The decision affirms the non-hierarchical, voluntary nature of the PCA and its limited jurisdiction in civil matters.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Michael Chastain appealed his conviction and indefinite suspension by Heritage Presbytery for divisive behavior, arising from his public letters to his congregation disagreeing with Session actions regarding an associate pastor call and a related Christian school controversy. The SJC denied the appeal (20-1), upholding the conviction and censure while finding procedural errors that did not rise to reversible level; a dissent by RE Frederick Neikirk argued the charge of 'divisive behavior' failed BCO 29-1's requirement that offenses be proven from Scripture.

artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission sustained the complaint of the Session of First Presbyterian Church, Augusta, finding that Savannah River Presbytery erred in annulling the Session's actions to dissolve the official relationship with eleven ruling elders. The SJC held that BCO 25-2 does not prohibit a Session from adding agenda items to congregational meetings called pursuant to petitions, and that BCO 24-6 does not prevent a Session from informing the congregation of this right and recommending its exercise.

artifacts.synopsis: RE Paul M. Wright filed a complaint against Eastern Carolina Presbytery regarding its response to a Reference from White Oak Presbyterian Church Session on a doctrinal issue. The SJC found the case judicially out of order because the Presbytery's action was advice only in response to a Reference for advice under BCO 41-1, and such advisory actions are not complainable under BCO 43. The Panel recommended the case be found out of order. Vote: 17 concurring, 1 dissenting (RE J. Howard Donahoe), 1 abstaining, 4 absent.
